anlamlar.en: to give something to a younger person or to people who live after you
ornekler: The ring was handed down from my grandmother.
These stories have been handed down for generations.

anlamlar.en: to give something to a person in authority
ornekler: Please hand in your homework by Friday.
He handed in his resignation.

anlamlar.en: to give something to each person in a group
ornekler: The teacher handed out the worksheets.
They were handing out leaflets in the street.

anlamlar.en: to give something or someone to another person, especially officially
ornekler: The thief was handed over to the police.
He handed over the keys to the new owner.

anlamlar.en: to wait or spend time somewhere without doing much
ornekler: Young people hang around the shopping center.
I hung around for an hour, but she never came.

anlamlar.en: to wait for a short time
ornekler: Hang on, I'll be ready in a minute.
Can you hang on while I get a pen?

anlamlar.en: to hold something tightly
ornekler: Hang on tight!
She hung on to the rope.

anlamlar.en: to end a phone call by putting the phone down
ornekler: He hung up before I could answer.
Don't hang up on me!

anlamlar.en: to put something such as clothes on a hook
ornekler: Hang up your coat in the hall.
She hung up her dress carefully.

anlamlar.en: to go towards a place
ornekler: Let's head for home.
The ship was heading for the coast.

anlamlar.en: to be likely to experience something bad
ornekler: The company is heading for disaster.
They're heading for trouble.

anlamlar.en: to receive a letter, phone call or message from someone
ornekler: Have you heard from your brother lately?
I look forward to hearing from you.

anlamlar.en: to know about someone or something
ornekler: I've never heard of him.
Have you heard of this band?

anlamlar.en: to help someone, especially by doing part of their work or giving them money
ornekler: My parents helped me out when I lost my job.
Can you help out in the kitchen?

anlamlar.en: to criticize or attack someone who has criticized or attacked you
ornekler: The minister hit back at his critics.
If he hits you, don't hit back.

anlamlar.en: to stop yourself from showing a feeling or doing something
ornekler: She held back her tears.
He held back from saying what he really thought.

anlamlar.en: to stop someone or something from developing or making progress
ornekler: Lack of money is holding the project back.
Don't let fear hold you back.

anlamlar.en: to wait for a short time
ornekler: Hold on, I'll get my coat.
Can you hold on a minute?

anlamlar.en: to hold something firmly
ornekler: Hold on tight!
She held on to the rail.

anlamlar.en: to make someone or something late
ornekler: Sorry I'm late – I was held up in traffic.
The flight was held up by bad weather.

anlamlar.en: to rob a person or place using a weapon
ornekler: Two men held up the bank.
The shop was held up last night.

anlamlar.en: to raise something or support something
ornekler: She held up her hand.
The roof is held up by four columns.

anlamlar.en: to move or do things more quickly
ornekler: Hurry up, we're going to miss the bus!
Can you hurry up in the bathroom?

anlamlar.en: to take part in an activity with other people
ornekler: Everyone joined in the singing.
Can I join in the game?

anlamlar.en: to interrupt a conversation
ornekler: Can I jump in here?
He always jumps in before I finish.

anlamlar.en: to not go near someone or something, or to stop someone going near
ornekler: Keep away from the fire!
Keep the medicine away from children.

anlamlar.en: to make someone stay inside
ornekler: The teacher kept us in after school.
They kept him in hospital for a week.

anlamlar.en: to not go onto an area
ornekler: Keep off the grass.
Please keep off the wet floor.

anlamlar.en: to continue doing something, or to do something many times
ornekler: She kept on asking questions.
Keep on walking until you reach the bridge.

anlamlar.en: to not enter a place, or to prevent someone from entering
ornekler: The sign said "Danger – keep out".
We put up a fence to keep the dogs out.

anlamlar.en: to move or do something at the same speed as someone else
ornekler: Slow down, I can't keep up!
She works so fast that nobody can keep up with her.

anlamlar.en: to continue doing something or make something continue at the same level
ornekler: Keep up the good work!
It's hard to keep up the payments.

anlamlar.en: to know about the most recent news or developments
ornekler: I try to keep up with the news.
It's hard to keep up with technology.

anlamlar.en: to start a football match
ornekler: The game kicks off at three o'clock.
What time does the match kick off?

anlamlar.en: to start an event or activity
ornekler: The festival kicks off with a concert.
Let's kick off the meeting with some good news.

anlamlar.en: to force someone to leave a place or organization
ornekler: He was kicked out of school.
His landlord kicked him out.

anlamlar.en: to destroy a building or wall
ornekler: They knocked down the old factory.
The houses will be knocked down next year.

anlamlar.en: to hit someone with a vehicle and make them fall
ornekler: She was knocked down by a car.
A cyclist was knocked down outside the school.

anlamlar.en: to make someone unconscious
ornekler: The boxer was knocked out in the third round.
The blow knocked him out.

anlamlar.en: to defeat a team so they cannot continue in a competition
ornekler: Our team was knocked out in the semi-final.
They knocked out last year's champions.

anlamlar.en: to hit something and make it fall
ornekler: The cat knocked over a vase.
Careful, you'll knock over your glass.

anlamlar.en: to officially state rules or principles
ornekler: The rules are laid down by the committee.
The law lays down strict limits.

anlamlar.en: to put something down
ornekler: She laid the baby down in the bed.
The soldiers laid down their weapons.

anlamlar.en: to stop employing someone because there is not enough work
ornekler: The factory laid off 200 workers.
He was laid off last month.

anlamlar.en: to arrange or spread something out
ornekler: She laid out the clothes on the bed.
The garden is laid out beautifully.

anlamlar.en: to explain something clearly and in detail
ornekler: The report lays out a plan for the future.
He laid out his ideas at the meeting.

anlamlar.en: to leave a place without taking something with you
ornekler: I left my umbrella behind on the train.
Don't leave anything behind.

anlamlar.en: to make progress faster than someone
ornekler: Small companies are being left behind.
He was left behind by the rest of the class.

anlamlar.en: to not include someone or something
ornekler: You left out a word in this sentence.
She felt left out because nobody spoke to her.

anlamlar.en: to disappoint someone by not doing what they expected
ornekler: I promised to help, and I won't let you down.
I feel let down by my friends.

anlamlar.en: to allow someone or something to enter
ornekler: Open the door and let the dog in.
The windows let in a lot of light.

anlamlar.en: to not punish someone, or to give them only a small punishment
ornekler: The police let him off with a warning.
I'll let you off this time.

anlamlar.en: to make something such as a bomb or firework explode
ornekler: They let off fireworks at midnight.
Someone let off a bomb.

anlamlar.en: to allow someone or something to leave a place
ornekler: Let the cat out, please.
He was let out of prison last year.

anlamlar.en: to make a sound
ornekler: She let out a scream.
He let out a sigh of relief.

anlamlar.en: to move into a position in which your body is flat, usually to sleep or rest
ornekler: I'm going to lie down for an hour.
Lie down on the bed and relax.

anlamlar.en: to make something bright with light, or to become bright
ornekler: Fireworks lit up the sky.
The city lights up at night.

anlamlar.en: to suddenly look happy
ornekler: Her face lit up when she saw him.
His eyes lit up at the idea.

anlamlar.en: to have a particular amount of money to buy things
ornekler: It's hard to live on such a small salary.
They live on $500 a month.

anlamlar.en: to eat a particular type of food
ornekler: Pandas live on bamboo.
As students we lived on pasta.

anlamlar.en: to continue to exist
ornekler: His memory will live on.
The tradition lives on today.

anlamlar.en: to be as good as people expected
ornekler: The film didn't live up to my expectations.
He's trying to live up to his father's reputation.

anlamlar.en: to lock all the doors and windows of a building
ornekler: Don't forget to lock up when you leave.
They locked up the shop and went home.

anlamlar.en: to put someone in prison
ornekler: He was locked up for ten years.
They should lock him up!

anlamlar.en: to stop using a computer system by giving a command
ornekler: Remember to log off when you finish.
I logged off and went to bed.

anlamlar.en: to stop being connected to a computer system or website
ornekler: Don't forget to log out of your account.
The system logs you out after ten minutes.

anlamlar.en: to take care of someone or something
ornekler: Who's looking after the children?
You should look after your health.

anlamlar.en: to think about what will happen in the future
ornekler: It's time to look ahead to next year.
We must look ahead and plan.

anlamlar.en: to visit a place and look at the things in it
ornekler: We spent the afternoon looking around the town.
Can I look around the house?

anlamlar.en: to turn your eyes towards someone or something
ornekler: Look at that beautiful bird!
She looked at me and smiled.

anlamlar.en: to think about or study a subject or problem
ornekler: We need to look at all the options.
The doctor looked at my knee.

anlamlar.en: to think about something that happened in the past
ornekler: Looking back, I should have studied harder.
She looked back on her childhood with pleasure.

anlamlar.en: to think that someone is less important than you
ornekler: He looks down on people who didn't go to university.
Don't look down on others.

anlamlar.en: to try to find someone or something
ornekler: I'm looking for my keys.
She's looking for a new job.

anlamlar.en: to feel happy and excited about something that is going to happen
ornekler: I'm looking forward to the holidays.
I look forward to hearing from you.

anlamlar.en: to examine the facts about a problem or situation
ornekler: The police are looking into the case.
I'll look into the matter.

anlamlar.en: to watch something happening without taking part
ornekler: A crowd looked on as the firefighters worked.
She looked on in horror.

anlamlar.en: to watch carefully for someone or something
ornekler: Look out for pickpockets in the market.
Look out for my sister at the party.

anlamlar.en: to take care of someone and protect them
ornekler: Older children should look out for younger ones.
He always looks out for his friends.

anlamlar.en: to examine something quickly
ornekler: Can you look over my essay?
He looked over the contract before signing it.

anlamlar.en: to read something quickly
ornekler: I looked through the newspaper.
She looked through her notes before the test.

anlamlar.en: to try to find a piece of information in a book or on a computer
ornekler: Look up the word in a dictionary.
I looked up the train times online.

anlamlar.en: to become better
ornekler: Things are finally looking up.
Business is looking up.

anlamlar.en: to raise your eyes
ornekler: She looked up from her book.
He looked up and saw the plane.

anlamlar.en: to admire and respect someone
ornekler: I've always looked up to my older brother.
Children need someone to look up to.

anlamlar.en: to not have an advantage or opportunity that others have
ornekler: Small farmers lose out to big companies.
If you don't apply, you'll lose out.
